subject: general
question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article at ₹5,960. Find the cost price if after allowing a discount of 9% he still gains 30% on the cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relationship between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**.

Ratio **CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)**.

CP : MP = (100 − 9) : (100 + 30) = 91 : 130.

Unitary method: 130 units = ₹5,960 ⇒ 1 unit = 5960 ÷ 130 = 45.846.

91 units = 91 × (5960 ÷ 130) = 7 × (5960 ÷ 10) = 7 × 596 = ₹4,172.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,172.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹5,960, **Discount** = 9%, **Profit** = 30%.
Formulas: **SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100** | **CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + P%)**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/471ae8307f84808843dcf8863d6f11c1502c19715f586dba90273dac9cc09420.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Selling Price (SP)** = 5960 × (100 − 9) ÷ 100
⇒ SP = 5960 × 0.91 = ₹5,423.6
⇒ Now, use SP to find **Cost Price (CP)**
⇒ CP = (5423.6 × 100) ÷ (100 + 30)
⇒ CP = 542360 ÷ 130 = ₹4,172.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,172.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Profit and CP Relationship

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. SP = CP + Profit.
